title: Borel and Analytic Sets, Perfect Sets, and Determinacy

items.title: Cantor sequence space
items.statement: In ZF, C is the subset of Baire sequence space consisting of functions with values in {0,1}, with its cylinder topology. The zero sequence witnesses nonemptiness.
items.proof_strategy: Definition; binary cylinders inherit the topology from Baire cylinders. No arbitrary product-nonemptiness principle is used.

items.title: Trees and their bodies
items.statement: For a set E, a tree is an initial-segment-closed subset of E^{<omega}; the empty tree is permitted. Its body is the set of x in E^omega all of whose finite restrictions lie in T. Pruned means every node has a proper extension. No equivalence with existence of branches is asserted for arbitrary E without choice.
items.proof_strategy: Definition; form the finite function sets by Replacement and Union. This is a general tree, not the finitely branching tree notion.
source_support: https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/math512/dst.pdf — Lemma 1.14 and Definition 1.15; general-alphabet extension also in Buffard–Levrel–Mayo opening definitions

items.title: Closed subsets of Baire space are tree bodies
items.statement: In ZF, F subset N^N is closed iff F=[T] for some tree on N. Take T to be finite prefixes of members of F; T is pruned if F is nonempty, and empty if F is empty.
items.proof_strategy: For a tree body, every excluded branch has a prefix outside T, giving an open complementary cylinder. Conversely every cylinder about a point of [T] meets F; if the point were outside closed F a disjoint cylinder would contradict this. Prefix extension uses a witness from F at the single node under consideration, not a simultaneous choice.
source_support: https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/math512/dst.pdf — Lemma 1.14(ii), Definition 1.15

items.title: Analytic and coanalytic sets by closed projection
items.statement: For a Polish space X, call A analytic when A is the X-projection of a closed subset of X times N^N; call its complement coanalytic. Empty sets are allowed. Equivalent Borel-image and continuous-image descriptions are separate outstanding theorems.
items.proof_strategy: Definition via closed projection. Do not silently appeal to the Borel-image equivalence before it is supplied.

items.title: Synchronous trees and projection bodies
items.statement: A synchronous tree on N times N is a set of pairs (s,t) of equally long finite sequences, closed under simultaneous restrictions. Its body consists of pairs of branches; its projection consists of first coordinates admitting a second-coordinate branch.
items.proof_strategy: Definition; preserve equal-length convention in all section trees.

items.title: Analytic subsets of Baire space have tree projections
items.statement: In ZF, A subset N^N is analytic in the closed-projection convention iff A=p[T] for a synchronous tree T. For each x, T_x={t:(x restricted to length(t),t) in T}; then x in A iff [T_x] is nonempty.
items.proof_strategy: Repeat the cylinder-complement proof on pairs of coordinates; every product basic neighbourhood refines a pair of cylinders of equal length. Project the resulting closed body. This proof needs no Borel-image theorem, rank theorem, or choice.

items.title: Gale–Stewart games and strategies
items.statement: Let T be a nonempty pruned tree on a nonempty set E and A subset [T]. Players I and II choose legal moves at even and odd positions, respectively. I wins iff the resulting branch belongs to A. A strategy assigns a legal move at every position of its parity; it wins iff every consistent branch is won. Determined means one player has a winning strategy. General-alphabet strategy existence is not automatic in ZF. The topology on [T] has cylinders [T]_p={x in [T]:p is a prefix of x}; empty cylinders are allowed. Cylinders are clopen: the complement at depth len(p) is the union of the other depth-len(p) cylinders.
items.proof_strategy: Definition with full-position strategies. Marker uses opponent-history strategies on the full tree; translate by simulation when citing his formulation.
source_support: https://arxiv.org/html/2401.09659v1 — Opening definitions, before Lemma 1; compare Marker Definitions 6.1–6.3

items.title: Axiom of determinacy for natural-number games
items.statement: AD asserts that for every subset A of N^N the game on N^{<omega} with payoff A is determined. This definition does not assert AD, AD implies unrestricted DC, or compatibility with AC.
items.proof_strategy: Definition. Conditional regularity items must use a separately audited ZF+AD or ZF+AD+DC proof and must not inherit AC-based proofs.

items.title: Game trees with terminal taboos
items.statement: A nonempty tree T may have terminal nodes partitioned into taboos for I and II. Reaching a taboo loses for the named player; infinite play has payoff A subset [T]. Finite plays are terminal nodes. Strategies are defined only at nonterminal positions. The space of all maximal plays has cylinders consisting of the terminal or infinite plays extending p; a terminal cylinder is a singleton. The infinite-play subspace [T] is closed, since its complement is the union of the terminal singleton cylinders. Payoff complexity is always measured in [T]. Fixed-history subgames retain the original parity and force every earlier move.
items.proof_strategy: Definition. Do not identify topological complexity in the infinite-play subspace with complexity in the space including terminal plays without proof. Cylinder intersections are empty or the longer cylinder, so arbitrary unions form a topology; [T] is closed by the displayed complementary union.
source_support: https://arxiv.org/html/2401.09659v1 — Definitions preceding Lemma 1

items.title: The countable Borel hierarchy and its limit convention
items.statement: For a topological space X, put Sigma^0_1(X)=the open sets; Pi^0_alpha(X)={X\A:A in Sigma^0_alpha(X)}; for 1<alpha<omega_1 let Sigma^0_alpha consist of countable unions of sets from the union of Pi^0_beta over 1<=beta<alpha. Delta^0_alpha is the intersection of the two classes. The least sigma-algebra containing the open sets is B(X). No fixed-rank strictness, cardinality, or monotonicity on arbitrary spaces is asserted here.
items.proof_strategy: Use set-length recursion on omega_1: from earlier classes form their union, its omega-indexed sequences and their unions; at stage 1 use the supplied topology. Complements are taken in the fixed ambient X. All values are subsets of P(X); extend the rule to malformed histories by a fixed empty value, as required by the recursion schema. The intersection of all sigma-algebras containing the topology defines B(X).
source_support: https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/math512/dst.pdf — Definition 2.4, printed p14; Martin 1985 p451 (same positive-rank convention)

items.title: Metric Borel hierarchy inclusions and fixed-rank operations
items.statement: For a metrizable X in ZFC and 1<=alpha<beta<omega_1, Sigma_alpha union Pi_alpha is contained in Delta_beta. At every positive rank Sigma is closed under countable unions and finite intersections, Pi under countable intersections and finite unions, and Delta under complements and finite unions/intersections. No countable-basis or strictness hypothesis is needed.
items.proof_strategy: Fix a compatible metric. Every open U is a countable union of closed sets F_n={x: for all y outside U, d(x,y)>=1/(n+1)}; each F_n is closed by the triangle inequality, and the metric neighbourhood condition gives U=union F_n, including U=X and empty U. Open sets are also countable intersections of themselves. This gives the rank-one to rank-two inclusions. Induct on beta: for alpha>1 each lower-Pi representation of a Sigma_alpha set is also a legal Sigma_beta representation; for alpha=1 use the base inclusion and that representation. Complementation gives same-type Pi inclusion; a constant union promotes Pi_alpha to Sigma_beta, and duality gives Sigma_alpha to Pi_beta. For fixed-rank operations, the rank-one case is topology. At alpha>1 select countable representations using AC and flatten the omega-by-omega union via a fixed diagonal enumeration. For a finite intersection distribute across these unions; each intersected pair of lower Pi sets can be raised to the maximum of its two positive ranks, still below alpha, and remains Pi at that rank by the inductive hypothesis. Complementation gives the dual and Delta conclusions. Empty finite intersections/unions are X/empty, which belong at every rank.
source_support: https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/math512/dst.pdf — Lemma 2.5(i) and Lemma 2.6(i–iii), printed pp15–16 (PDF pages 15–16); source numbering in previous notes was one page low

items.title: Well-founded Borel evaluation codes
items.statement: Fix a topological space X and an enumerated basis (U_n). A code is a nonempty tree T on N, with each node labelled leaf(n), complement, or union. A leaf has no children; a complement node has exactly child 0; a union node has any set of children indexed by a subset of N, including none. Require the immediate-child relation (child precedes parent) to be well-founded. Thus a union node with no children codes the empty set. Invalid labelled trees have no assigned evaluation.
items.proof_strategy: Definition on a set of labelled subsets of N^{<omega}. Well-foundedness is part of the code, not a claim derived from an arbitrary-alphabet no-branch principle. Leaf values are the specified basis opens; countable unions and complements will be evaluated only by the next lemma.
source_support: https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/math512/dst.pdf — Definitions 7.1–7.2, printed pp62–63; nodewise labels and empty union made explicit

items.title: Existence and uniqueness of Borel-code evaluation
items.statement: Each code has a unique evaluation E:T->P(X), assigning U_n at leaf(n), X minus the child value at complement nodes, and the union of child values at union nodes. Its root value is Borel. Conversely, in ZFC every Borel subset of a space with an enumerated basis has a code. The evaluation and forward Borel conclusion are ZF assertions.
items.proof_strategy: Apply relation recursion with the immediate children as predecessors. Make the functional rule total on arbitrary predecessor functions by replacing any non-subset-of-X value with empty before complementing or taking the union; values actually constructed are subsets of X. Well-founded induction proves both uniqueness and Borelness. The family of root values contains each basic open and all opens (union the subfamily of basis elements contained in the open). It is closed under complement by adding a root with one child. For a sequence of coded sets choose codes using AC; graft their tagged trees below a union root. The new relation is well-founded: in any nonempty subset meeting a constituent subtree, a minimal member of that intersection is minimal globally; otherwise only the root remains. Thus root values form a sigma-algebra and include every Borel set. Empty unions, empty X and leaf labels are covered without inventing an empty root.
source_support: https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/math512/dst.pdf — Definitions 7.1–7.2 and Exercise 7.3, printed pp62–63; full local recursion proof supplies the exercise

items.title: Cantor and Baire sequence spaces and coordinate codings
items.statement: In ZF, Cantor and Baire sequence spaces are Polish for d(x,y)=0 if equal and 2^{-m-1} at the first differing coordinate m. Cantor space is compact and has no isolated points. Fixed diagonal enumerations identify N^N with (N^N)^N and 2^N with (2^N)^N by homeomorphisms. The map x -> 0^{x(0)}1 0^{x(1)}1 ... is a homeomorphism from Baire space onto the subspace of Cantor space with infinitely many 1s, whose complement is countable.
items.proof_strategy: The common-prefix inequality proves the ultrametric law. A Cauchy sequence has each coordinate eventually constant, and the uniquely specified coordinate limits give its limit without choice. Eventually-zero sequences form an explicitly enumerable dense set. For compactness, if an open cover has no finite subcover, the empty cylinder has no finite subcover; recursively choose the least binary child with that property. The resulting branch lies in one cover member, which contains a prefix cylinder, a contradiction. Flipping a later bit proves absence of isolated points. Diagonal coordinate pairing and its inverse preserve cylinder neighbourhoods, hence are homeomorphisms. Block coding and decoding the gaps between successive 1s are continuous at every coded point. The exceptional eventually-zero binary sequences have a finite prefix code, yielding an injection into N.

items.title: Borel hierarchy exhaustion and preservation by continuous pullback
items.statement: In ZFC, for every topological space X, B(X) is the union of Sigma^0_alpha(X) over 1<=alpha<omega_1. Continuous inverse image preserves Sigma^0_alpha, Pi^0_alpha and Delta^0_alpha at the same positive rank. For Y a subspace, Sigma^0_alpha(Y) and Pi^0_alpha(Y) are exactly traces of the corresponding classes on X. The preimage implication needs no choice beyond the given rank representation; the trace lifting and exhaustion are stated under AC.
items.proof_strategy: Every hierarchy class lies in B(X) by ordinal induction. If A is Sigma_alpha, its complement is Pi_alpha and hence Sigma_{alpha+1} by a constant sequence; also A is Pi_{alpha+1}. For a countable family A_n in the union, choose rank witnesses alpha_n (least ranks suffice), bound all alpha_n+2 below omega_1 using countable-choice boundedness, and express union A_n as a union of lower Pi levels. Thus the union of all levels is a sigma-algebra. Continuous pullback commutes with complement and countable union, giving rank preservation by induction, including limit ranks. For traces, open sets lift by definition of the subspace topology; lift complements relative to X and countably many lower-rank constituents using AC. No assertion about traces of Delta classes is made.
source_support: https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~marker/math512/dst.pdf — Lemma 2.5(i–ii), Lemma 2.6(iv), Exercise 2.8(a), printed pp14–15; local exhaustion argument fills the abbreviated sigma-algebra step

items.title: Universal Borel sets and strictness on Cantor space
items.statement: In ZFC, for every separable metric X and every positive countable alpha there are Sigma_alpha- and Pi_alpha-universal subsets U_alpha,V_alpha of C times X, where C=2^N. Universal means every set in the indicated class on X is a section at some c in C. For each alpha, Pi_alpha(C) is not contained in Sigma_alpha(C), and conversely. The same strictness holds on every metrizable space containing a subspace homeomorphic to C; application to all uncountable Polish spaces awaits the local perfect-set theorem.
items.proof_strategy: A countable dense set and positive rational radii provide an enumerated metric basis W_n. Put U_1={(c,x):exists n,c(n)=1 and x in W_n}; its sections exhaust the opens, including empty. Complement to obtain V_1. At alpha>1 fix a nondecreasing sequence of positive beta_n<alpha cofinal in the sense sup(beta_n+1)=alpha; for successor ranks take the predecessor constantly. Identify c with a sequence c_n and put U_alpha={(c,x):exists n,(c_n,x) in V_beta_n}. Coordinate pullback and union give the rank. Given a union of lower-Pi sets, inject its terms successively into indices n with beta_n at least their ranks, which exist arbitrarily late; put empty sets at unused indices and choose their universal parameters using AC. Complement for V_alpha. This avoids assuming the original nth constituent already has rank <=beta_n. Recursion is on omega_1 with all candidates subsets of fixed C times X, so the selections are set-sized. On C diagonal inverse image gives D_alpha={c:(c,c) not in U_alpha} in Pi_alpha; a Sigma_alpha section representation at d would give d in D iff d not in D. Take complements for the other difference. Homeomorphism and the earlier trace lifting lemma transfer failure of equality to any containing metrizable space.

items.title: Terminal reachability and residual positions
items.statement: In ZFC, for a game tree with taboos, let W_P be the positions from which player P can force a terminal taboo for the other player, with no infinite play counted as a success. W_I and W_II are disjoint. At a nonterminal P-position, membership in W_P is equivalent to some immediate child belonging to W_P; at an opponent-position, it is equivalent to every immediate child belonging to W_P. Winning reachability strategies can be fixed simultaneously for all members of W_P.
items.proof_strategy: All strategy sets are sets of functions on subsets of the set tree. AC supplies default legal moves and one winning strategy at every winning position. Restriction proves the necessary child conditions. Conversely at a P-position take a winning child; at an opponent-position paste the selected winning child strategies according to the opponent's first move. Any resulting play uses one selected strategy and so terminates with the required taboo. Opposite winning strategies have a unique compatible maximal play, constructed recursively until termination or through omega; it cannot be taboo for both players, proving disjointness. The same argument works at either parity with the history fixed, not by swapping player labels.

items.title: Taboo games reduce to pruned residual games
items.statement: In ZFC, either the root is terminal-reachability winning for one player, or S={p in T: every prefix of p avoids W_I union W_II} is a nonempty pruned subtree of T. In the latter case any winning strategy for G(A intersect [S];S) extends to a winning strategy for G(A;T), for every A subset [T]. Continuous restriction preserves each Borel payoff level. Consequently determinacy at each such level for pruned trees implies it for trees with taboos; the reverse follows by taking no taboos.
items.proof_strategy: If the root is winning, its reachability strategy wins regardless of A. Otherwise S contains the root and is prefix closed by its definition. At p in S of parity P no child is in W_P. Some child avoids W_other, since otherwise p is in W_other by the all-children clause. That child avoids both sets; it is in S. Thus S is pruned and has no original terminal nodes. Extend a strategy for P on S by following it until the opponent first exits S. The exit child is outside W_other (otherwise its parent is in W_other by the some-child clause), hence is in W_P. Switch to the fixed P reachability strategy there. Opponent exits therefore win for P; no exit gives an original infinite play in [S] with unchanged payoff. Totalize at inconsistent positions by fixed legal moves. Restriction of cylinders shows the inclusion [S]->[T] is continuous; rank preservation is by direct induction on the displayed complement/union expressions. The false deletion T\(W_I union W_II) is never used.

items.title: Open and closed Gale–Stewart games are determined
items.statement: In ZFC, every open or closed payoff on a nonempty pruned tree over a set alphabet yields a determined game, with either player allowed to move first at a fixed history. The same holds with terminal taboos, with open/closed referring to the infinite-play subspace.
items.proof_strategy: On a pruned tree with open payoff A for P, let U be the positions whose branch cylinders are contained in A. Let W be the positions from which P can force a visit to U in finitely many moves. The reachability pasting argument gives: at P-nodes outside W all children avoid W; at opponent-nodes outside W some child avoids W. If the initial position is in W, a witnessing strategy wins A; otherwise the opponent chooses such avoiding children using AC. The resulting branch never visits U, hence is outside A since A is open. For a closed payoff apply this argument to the open complement and its winning player. For taboos apply the earlier residual reduction, using continuity of the inclusion. This argument chooses entire winning strategies when pasting; it does not mistake pointwise strategy existence for a choice-free selection.

items.title: Game coverings, k-coverings and unraveling
items.statement: A covering of a taboo tree T is (S,pi,phi), with S a taboo tree; pi:S->T preserves length and prefixes, and pi(s) taboo for P implies s taboo for P. The induced map on infinite branches is also called pi. phi maps total strategies on S to strategies for the same player on T; its values at positions of length <n depend only on input values at positions of length <n. For every sigma and every maximal play x consistent with phi(sigma), some maximal y consistent with sigma satisfies pi(y) prefix x, and either pi(y)=x or y is taboo for the player of sigma. A k-covering has identical nodes and taboo labels at lengths <=k, identity pi there, and identity strategy restrictions at positions of length <k. It unravels A if pi^{-1}(A) is clopen in [S].
items.proof_strategy: Prefix union defines the map on infinite plays and preserves length. The preimage of a cylinder is a union of cylinders at the same depth, proving continuity directly. Finite lifted plays may project to nonterminal positions, which is why the losing-short-lift exception is necessary. This triple convention uses existential lifts; it does not assert coherence of independently chosen witnesses.

items.title: Winning strategies descend through game coverings
items.statement: For a covering (S,pi,phi) of T and any A subset [T], if sigma wins G(pi^{-1}(A);S), phi(sigma) wins G(A;T), for the same player.
items.proof_strategy: Lift an arbitrary phi(sigma)-consistent maximal play x to y. Since sigma wins, y is not taboo for its player; the lifting axiom therefore gives pi(y)=x. If y is infinite, payoff membership transfers by definition of preimage. If y is finite, x is also a finite maximal play and hence terminal; the direction pi(y) taboo for Q implies y taboo for Q forces x and y to have the same taboo label. This uses terminality of x; it does not reverse taboo reflection for an arbitrary finite lifted node.

items.title: Composition and continuity of game coverings
items.statement: Identity maps are coverings; composition (R,pi_1 composed pi_2,phi_1 composed phi_2) of two coverings is a covering. A k_1-covering composed with a k_2-covering is a min(k_1,k_2)-covering. Induced branch maps are continuous, and continuous covering preimages preserve already achieved clopenness.
items.proof_strategy: Lift a target play first along the lower covering for phi_2(sigma), then along the upper for sigma. Projection of the final lift is a prefix of the original play. If both equalities hold, it is equal. If the second lift shortens, it is taboo for the player of sigma. If only the first shortens, its finite play is taboo for that same player; the second lift is either a losing short lift or projects exactly to that terminal play and hence inherits its taboo by reflection. Prefix/length preservation and strategy locality compose. Identity up to the minimum depth is literal. Cylinder preimages prove continuity, then the preimages of an open set and its open complement are open.

items.title: Stabilizing systems of game coverings have inverse limits
items.statement: In ZFC, let T_i (i in omega) be taboo trees and C_{j,i} be k-coverings for i<=j, with identity diagonal and coherent position and strategy maps under composition. Suppose for every n there is i_n such that every C_{j,l} with j>=l>=i_n is an n-covering. There is a taboo tree T_infty and k-coverings C_{infty,i} with coherent position and strategy maps C_{infty,i}=C_{j,i} composed C_{infty,j}. No specified coherent lift function is part of the triple convention.
items.proof_strategy: Choose increasing stabilization indices i_n. Define nodes and taboo labels at depth <=n by the stabilized finite tree. They agree on overlaps. A nonterminal limit node has a child by examining one additional stabilized level. Define pi and phi to stage i by composing from any stage beyond both i and the stabilization depth; coherence and locality give independence and compatible restrictions. For a limit strategy s put s_i=phi_{infty,i}(s). Starting with a play x_j consistent with s_j, choose recursively x_{i+1} lifting x_i along C_{i+1,i} for s_{i+1}, never independently from x_j. All choices are among subsets of the union of the set-sized play spaces, so AC supplies a single choice function. Once depth n is stabilized, these lifts agree through depth n: a shorter lift below n would be a terminal node at a common finite level and its image could not be a proper prefix of the earlier maximal play. Hence the eventual prefixes define a maximal limit play y consistent with s. If all x_i are infinite, pi(y)=x_j. If a finite lift ever occurs, later lengths are nonincreasing and eventually constant; its limiting taboo label is the label of the strategy player whenever any projection was a proper prefix. Reflection preserves that label through exact lifts; further proper lifts again have that label. If none was proper, y projects exactly to x_j. This proves both finite and infinite lifting cases. The maps commute by their finite definitions.

items.title: Closed and open payoffs admit unraveling covers
items.statement: In ZFC, for every taboo tree T, every open or closed A subset [T], and every k in omega, some k-covering of T unravels A. The alphabet may grow to a set containing subsets of the original tree; it is not restricted to countable alphabets.
items.proof_strategy: It suffices to treat closed A and even k>=the requested depth. Keep the tree and labels unchanged through k. At p of length k, I plays (a,X), where a is legal and X is any subset of Z: the nonterminal q strictly extending p^a with [T_q] disjoint from A, minimal among strict extensions with that property. Preserve an original terminal p^a and its label. Otherwise II either accepts, playing (1,b), or challenges r in X, playing (2,r,b) with b=r(k+1). In the accept branch follow T until the first original terminal or Z-node; preserve the original terminal label and make a Z-node taboo for II iff it belongs to X. No descendants of these new terminal nodes are retained. In the challenge branch force the history to r, then follow T with original taboos. Erasing decorations defines pi and reflects original taboos. Infinite accept plays never meet Z and therefore lie in A by closedness; infinite challenge plays extend r and lie outside A. Thus lifted membership is decided by the accept/challenge bit. For I's strategy, simulate acceptance until Z; at r outside X use the resulting I-taboo short lift and a fixed default continuation, while at r in X resimulate as if II challenged r and follow the strategy from r onward. The earlier forced segment to r is compatible with this retrospective lift. For II's strategy at p^a, set Y={r in Z: no response to any (a,X) challenges r}. The response to Y must accept, since a challenge would belong to Y and simultaneously witness exclusion from Y. Simulate this response. At r in Y use its II-taboo short lift and defaults. At r outside Y choose X_r with response challenging r, resimulate that challenge, and follow the strategy thereafter; before r the forced segment is compatible. Preserve all original terminal cases, including those before decoration. At every position of length m<k preserve the input strategy value, including inconsistent histories. Fix legal default moves independent of strategies, and at lengths m>=k assign them after the first inconsistent own move or losing short lift. Values at a position of length m then use only input responses at lengths <=m: before k they are identical; at k+1 the Y table has depth k+1; later simulations query only positions of the current depth. items.title: Coding strategies and their compatible plays
items.statement: In ZF, for either player on the full natural-number game tree, the set of all strategies is in bijection with N^N. items.title: Perfect-set game strategy dichotomy on Cantor space
items.statement: For A subset C in ZF, consider the game in which I plays any finite binary block (empty permitted) and II plays one bit in each round; I wins iff the concatenated infinite sequence lies in A. An I winning strategy yields a continuous injection C->A with compact, closed, no-isolated-point image. A II winning strategy yields an injection A->N. The game is an integer game by fixed block codes; an illegal II bit loses immediately.
items.proof_strategy: Given I strategy sigma, map z in C to the outcome against the bits of z. The first different opponent bit gives different outcomes; each output prefix depends on finitely many input bits because at least one bit is added every round. For each cylinder in the domain, only finitely many histories of bounded rounds occur; its image and the image of its complementary finitely many cylinders are compact by pulling back an open cover to the binary compactness proof, hence closed in the metric codomain (a point outside a compact set can be separated by finitely many small balls). This proves that the inverse is continuous and that the image has no isolated point. For a II strategy tau and x in A, there must be a finite legal history h producing a prefix of x, ending before I move, from which every block t extending that prefix along x elicits a bit different from the next bit of x. If no such barrier existed, choose the least compatible block at each round to construct a tau-play yielding x, a contradiction. For fixed h at most one x has this barrier property: its successive next bits are 1 minus tau response to the already reconstructed remaining prefix (empty block for the first bit), always queried from the same h. Code finite histories by N and assign x its least barrier code, an injection. Retaining full histories, rather than only concatenated prefixes, handles a history-dependent tau.

items.title: Closed subspaces, products, and Baire parametrization
items.statement: In ZFC, finite products and closed subspaces of Polish spaces are Polish. Every nonempty Polish space is the continuous image of N^N. No map from nonempty Baire space onto the empty space is asserted.

For each branch choose points in U_prefix using AC; they form a Cauchy sequence, whose limit belongs to every U_prefix because the next closure lies inside it. Uniqueness follows from shrinking diameter. Every x follows the least child containing it, proving surjectivity. A common long prefix forces images into the same small set, proving continuity.

items.statement: In ZFC, for A subset Polish X, the following are equivalent: A is a closed projection from X times N^N; A is empty or a continuous image of N^N; A is a continuous image of a Borel subset of a Polish space; A is a projection of a Borel subset of Y times X for Polish Y. items.title: Baire property sigma-algebra and Borel regularity
items.statement: In ZFC, in every topological space X the sets with the Baire property form a sigma-algebra containing the Borel sets. Every meagre subset has the Baire property. Every set with the Baire property differs from both an F_sigma set and a G_delta set by a meagre set.

With AC selecting witnesses, a countable union of meagre sets is meagre by flattening countably many witness sequences. A closed F differs from its open interior by the closed nowhere dense F minus interior F. If A differs from open U by a meagre set, then X minus A differs from interior(X minus U) by that meagre set plus the nowhere dense boundary of U. Countable unions of A_n differ from union U_n by a subset of the union of their meagre errors. Hence the class is a sigma-algebra containing opens. For the last assertion put the error inside an F_sigma meagre set M by closing its nowhere dense witnesses. Then U minus M is G_delta, A is contained in U union M, and replace U by a closed set differing from it by its nowhere dense boundary to obtain an F_sigma upper envelope; the differences are meagre. The G_delta assertion here uses that open U itself is G_delta by repetition, so no metrizability is required.

items.title: The Souslin operation preserves the Baire property
items.statement: Assume AC. In a topological space X with a specified countable basis, every subset A has a Baire-property envelope H containing A such that H minus D is meagre for every Baire-property D containing A. The Souslin operation on any scheme of Baire-property sets has the Baire property. Consequently every analytic subset of a Polish space has the Baire property.
items.proof_strategy:
Assume AC, used to select countably many meagre witnesses and envelopes, never deduced from AD. For arbitrary A let U be the union of all basic opens V for which A intersect V is meagre. Its countable basis gives A intersect U meagre. Put F=X minus U and H=A union F. Then H differs from closed F by a meagre set, so H has the Baire property. If D has that property and contains A, put C=H minus D, which also has the property and lies in F. If C were nonmeagre, choose open O with C symmetric-difference O meagre. O must be nonmeagre. Since O minus C is meagre and C is disjoint from A, A intersect O is meagre. Every basic V contained in O therefore occurs in U, so O is contained in U, disjoint from C. This makes O=O minus C meagre, contradiction. Thus H is an envelope. This argument does not assume X itself is a Baire space.
For a scheme normalize by finite prefix intersections, retaining the empty-prefix term. Write E_s for the union of branch intersections over branches extending s; E_s is contained in A_s and E_s=union_k E_{s concatenated k}. Choose envelopes H_s of E_s. Set B_s=A_s intersect intersection_{t prefix s} H_t. Then E_s is contained in B_s, B_s is Baire-property, decreases along extensions, and remains an envelope of E_s since B_s is contained in H_s. The set C_s=B_s minus union_k B_{s concatenated k} is meagre by the envelope property. Hence C=union_s C_s is meagre. If x lies in B_empty minus C, choose recursively the least k with x in the next B_{s concatenated k}; the choice exists since x is outside C_s. This explicitly defines a branch f, without a dependent-choice step, and x belongs to every A_{f|n}, hence to S(A). Conversely S(A)=E_empty is contained in B_empty. Thus B_empty minus S(A) is a subset of C and is meagre, so S(A) has the Baire property. Empty X and empty schemes' values obey the same argument. Apply the earlier closed-scheme characterization to analytic sets; closed sets have the Baire property.

items.title: The Souslin operation preserves Lebesgue measurability
items.statement: Assume AC and n>=1. Every A subset R^n has a measurable envelope H containing A such that H minus D is null for every Lebesgue measurable D containing A. The Souslin operation on a scheme of Lebesgue measurable subsets of R^n is Lebesgue measurable. Every analytic subset of R^n is therefore Lebesgue measurable.
items.proof_strategy:
AC supplies the countably many hulls below and the inherited countable-choice hypotheses of the Lebesgue measure results. Cover R^n by Q_j=(-j,j]^n for positive integers j, each measurable of finite volume. For E_j=A intersect Q_j use the published hull theorem to choose a measurable G_j containing E_j with lambda(G_j)=lambda*(E_j)<infinity, and put H_j=G_j intersect Q_j. Monotonicity gives lambda(H_j)=lambda*(E_j). If D is measurable and contains A, then E_j is contained in H_j intersect D, so lambda(H_j intersect D)>=lambda*(E_j)=lambda(H_j). Splitting the finite-measure H_j into H_j intersect D and H_j minus D gives lambda(H_j minus D)=0. H=union_j H_j contains A and H minus D is null by countable subadditivity. This avoids subtracting two infinite measures; the infinite-mass hull alone is inadequate.
For a scheme (A_s), first replace values by finite prefix intersections. Let E_s be its branch tail union at s, so E_s subset A_s and E_s=union_k E_{s concatenated k}. Choose measurable envelopes H_s, and put B_s=A_s intersect intersection_{t prefix s} H_t. These are decreasing measurable envelopes of E_s. Since union_k B_{s concatenated k} is a measurable superset of E_s, C_s=B_s minus union_k B_{s concatenated k} is null. C=union_s C_s is null. Every x in B_empty minus C yields a branch by choosing the least child index k retaining x, and hence belongs to S(A). Thus S(A) is contained in B_empty and differs from it by a subset of C. Completeness of Lebesgue measure proves measurability, including empty values. Closed subsets of R^n are Borel and measurable by the published theorem, so the earlier closed-scheme representation proves the analytic consequence. No AD conclusion follows from this AC-based proof.

items.title: The Banach–Mazur category game on sequence spaces and the real line
items.statement: In ZF, let X be N^N, 2^N, or R, and A subset X. Fix a natural-number coding of finite strings or rational-endpoint bounded open intervals. In the sequence cases players alternately choose strictly increasing finite prefixes, the first nonempty; V_n is the cylinder of the nth prefix. For R choose nonempty rational open intervals V_n with closure(V_(n+1)) subset V_n and length(V_n)<1/(n+1). A fixed initial basic open V may be imposed by requiring closure(V_0) subset V in R, or V_0 subset V for cylinders. I wins exactly when the resulting point lies in A. In a coded natural-number game the first illegal move loses, regardless of later moves. There is always a legal extension.
items.proof_strategy: Finite strings are coded by length and repeated pairing (pair i,j by (i+j)(i+j+1)/2+j); rational pairs are coded using the published enumeration. Legal extension sets are subsets of N, so least legal moves exist without choice. In sequence spaces the union of strictly extending strings defines one point. In R the closures are nonempty nested bounded closed intervals with lengths tending to zero, so the nested-interval theorem gives a unique point; it lies in each V_n because the next closure lies inside V_n. Rational density provides arbitrarily small legal intervals. Adding the set of plays whose first illegal move belongs to II to the legal winning payoff defines a subset of N^N. A winning coded strategy cannot make a first illegal move against legal play: the opponent can extend legally using least moves. Restriction therefore gives a legal winning strategy. This uses the AD definition only when determinacy is later assumed, not any AC-based determinacy theorem.

items.title: Category-game strategies characterize meagreness and local comeagreness
items.statement: In ZF, for X=N^N, 2^N or R, II wins the category game with target A iff A is meagre in X. I wins iff A is comeagre in some nonempty basic open subset of X. Both statements hold relative to a fixed initial basic open set. Each winning strategy yields a specified sequence of closed nowhere dense witnesses. No determinacy assumption, AC or DC is used.
items.proof_strategy:
First, a specified sequence of nowhere dense witnesses may be replaced by its closures. If A is covered by (F_n), at turn n II chooses the least legal refinement disjoint from F_n. The resulting point avoids all F_n. Conversely let tau win for II. For each even-length legal history p consistent with tau, let V_p be its last open (X at the empty history). Put D_p=(X minus closure(V_p)) union the union of all response opens tau(p followed by W), for W a legal next move. This is open and dense: any open meeting V_p has a basic refinement W with closure inside that intersection in R (a proper cylinder refinement in sequence spaces), small enough for the current bound, and tau responds inside W. An open not meeting V_p either meets X minus closure(V_p), or would lie in its boundary; the latter has empty interior. Thus F_p=X minus D_p is closed nowhere dense. Enumerate all finite histories by their natural codes, inserting the empty set for irrelevant codes. If x avoids every F_p, recursively at the empty history and each subsequent tau-history choose the least next-move code W whose response contains x. Such a W exists from x in D_p and x in V_p. This constructs a full play with outcome x, so x is outside A. Hence A is covered by the explicit F_p sequence. This argument uses no assertion that every dense G_delta is nonempty.

For the I direction, let V_0 be I's first move under a winning strategy sigma. Thereafter reverse player names: old II moves first and old I responds, with target V_0 minus A. Apply the preceding response-open proof relative to V_0. The turn-dependent shrinking bound is shifted by one; the proof only requires arbitrarily small legal refinements and a bound tending to zero, so it applies verbatim. Thus V_0 minus A is meagre in V_0. Conversely, if A is comeagre in a basic V, first choose a legal basic V_0 inside V and then use the least refinements avoiding the successive closed witnesses on each I turn; the play ends in A. Meagreness in an open subspace transfers to the ambient space: a relatively nowhere dense subset N of V is nowhere dense in X, since every open meeting V has an open refinement in V avoiding its relative closure, while every open missing V misses N; points of closure(N) outside V lie in the boundary of V. The reverse restriction is immediate. Finally no nonempty basic open is meagre: against a purported sequence of closed nowhere dense witnesses choose least nested refinements avoiding them with the same length/diameter conditions; the resulting point remains in the initial open and avoids all witnesses. This is a direct ZF construction and supplies the nonemptiness needed for the next theorem.

items.title: AD implies the Baire property for subsets of sequence spaces and the real line
items.statement: In ZF+AD, every subset of N^N, 2^N, or R has the Baire property. The proof uses countable choice only for sets of codes in N^N, obtained from AD, and does not assume AC or infer unrestricted DC.
items.proof_strategy:
Fix A and let U be the union of all basic opens V on which A is comeagre. There are countably many such V. A closed set F is coded uniquely by the set of basic opens disjoint from F: its complement is their union. Thus a sequence of closed nowhere dense sets can be encoded by a binary array and then one Baire real using the explicit pairing from the game definition. For each basic V contributing to U, the set of codes of sequences covering V minus A is nonempty by the characterization and open-subspace transfer. For every other basic V use the singleton code of the all-empty sequence. Apply thm-ad-implies-countable-choice-for-baire-space to these sets of codes, and interleave the selected sequences by the fixed pairing. This gives an actual nowhere dense covering sequence for U minus A, rather than an unsupported countable union of existentially meagre sets.

Put E=A minus U. AD applied to the explicitly coded legal category game makes it determined. I cannot win: the characterization would make E comeagre in a nonempty basic V; then A is comeagre there, so V subset U, but E intersect V is empty. That would make V meagre in itself, contradicting the direct least-refinement Baire argument. Therefore II wins, and the explicit strategy-to-witness construction makes E meagre. Interleave this witness sequence with the one for U minus A. Their union covers A symmetric-difference U, proving the claim by the definition. Exactly the same coded-open argument works for rational intervals, so no unproved transfer homeomorphism from sequence space to R is invoked.

items.title: Choice gives a Bernstein set with no perfect-set, Baire or measure regularity
items.statement: Assume AC. There exists a Bernstein B subset R. Both B and its complement are uncountable, contain no nonempty perfect subset, have no Baire property, are not Lebesgue measurable and are not Borel. B has inner measure zero and has full outer measure in every nondegenerate bounded interval. Existence alone requires only a wellordering of R; the measure consequences here use the explicitly stronger AC hypothesis.
items.proof_strategy:
AC supplies a wellordering of R and countable choice (apply a choice function to the range of a sequence of nonempty sets and compose with the sequence). Apply the existing published real-line Bernstein existence theorem, which recursively picks least fresh points from continuum-sized perfect sets; no regularity of continuum is needed. By the Bernstein definition neither side contains a nonempty perfect set, and both sides are Bernstein. The existing published inner/outer-measure theorem and its nonmeasurability corollary now apply under countable choice to both sides. No sequence-space transfer or new existence theorem is assumed.

Here is the missing category argument, including its supporting perfect-set construction. Given a nonempty real open interval J and a specified sequence (F_n) of closed nowhere dense sets, construct a binary tree of rational open intervals: start with a bounded rational interval whose closure lies in J minus F_0; at each level choose the least rational quadruple yielding two nonempty child intervals with disjoint closures inside the parent minus F_(n+1), each of length <1/(n+2). Such a quadruple exists by nowhere density and rational density. Recursion with least codes requires no further choice. Let K be the intersection over levels of the finite unions of closed intervals. It is closed and bounded. Every binary branch has a unique limit by the nested-interval theorem and the reciprocal bound, and disjoint siblings give distinct limits. Every point of K determines such a branch uniquely; following a different sibling at arbitrarily large depth gives another K point arbitrarily near it. Thus K is a nonempty perfect set contained in J and avoiding every F_n. This proves a local Cantor-avoidance lemma rather than citing a later perfect-set theorem.

A meagre Bernstein B is impossible: close its nowhere dense witnesses and construct such K in (0,1) outside B. If B had the Baire property, write B symmetric-difference U subset union_n F_n with U open and F_n closed nowhere dense. If U is empty B would be meagre. Otherwise choose an interval J inside U; the same construction gives a perfect K subset J minus union_n F_n subset B, again impossible. The same proof applies to the complement. A countable subset is meagre by a singleton covering (a finite or empty set is padded), so both sides are uncountable. Finally every Borel subset of R has the Baire property by the earlier local sigma-algebra contract, whose countable witness choice is available from AC; hence neither side is Borel. AC is used for the initial wellorder and to cover the published measure/category choice hypotheses, not claimed to follow from AD.

items.title: A Hamel coefficient has dense graph and a nonmeasurable kernel
items.statement: Assume AC. Fix a Hamel basis B of R over Q and b in B. The coefficient map f=Lambda_b:R->Q subset R is additive, has dense graph, and is unbounded above and below on every nondegenerate interval and continuous nowhere. Its kernel W is not Lebesgue measurable; therefore f is not Lebesgue measurable. No assertion that every Hamel basis itself is nonmeasurable is made.
items.proof_strategy:
The published Hamel lemma supplies B, the unique additive Q-linear coefficient f, f(b)=1, its rational range, and a nonzero w in its kernel W. AC is used through that lemma's vector-space-basis/Zorn argument and to supply countable choice for Lebesgue measure. The subgroup Qw is dense: for any u<v pick a rational strictly between min(u/w,v/w) and max(u/w,v/w). Multiplication by w puts its multiple in (u,v), with order reversed when w<0. For rational q the fiber f^{-1}{q}=qb+W therefore meets every real interval. Every open rectangle (u,v) times (c,d) contains a graph point: choose rational q in (c,d) and then a point of qb+W in (u,v). Thus the graph is dense. Taking vertical intervals arbitrarily high or low proves unboundedness on each nondegenerate interval. For any x_0 and any delta>0, the rectangle (x_0-delta,x_0+delta) times (f(x_0)+2,f(x_0)+3) contains a graph point, contradicting the epsilon=1 continuity condition at x_0. This argument uses the existing coefficient supplier, not the B-page example as a dependency.

Suppose W measurable, and let W_m=W intersect [-m,m] for positive integers m. For distinct rational q,r the cosets qb+W and rb+W are disjoint, since f((q-r)b)=q-r. Enumerate the infinitely many rationals with |qb|<1 by retaining them from a fixed rational enumeration. Infinitude follows from rational density on (-1/|b|,1/|b|); b is nonzero since f(b)=1. All translates W_m+qb are disjoint and contained in [-m-1,m+1]. If lambda(W_m)=a>0, its finite value follows from the enclosing box; Archimedean choose N with Na>2m+2. The first N translates have measure Na by finite additivity and translation invariance, contradiction. Thus every W_m is null. Their union W is null by countable subadditivity, derived from countable additivity by disjointizing. But R is the countable union of the null cosets qb+W as q runs over Q, again impossible since [0,1] has measure one. Hence W is nonmeasurable. The singleton {0} is closed and Borel, so if f were Lebesgue measurable its inverse image W would be measurable, contradiction. This proves the claimed measure consequence locally without a Steinhaus or measurable-Cauchy supplier.

items.title: Dyadic coding supplies coin measure and its completed Lebesgue transfer
items.statement: In ZF there is an injective binary coding b:[0,1)->C=2^N whose cylinder inverse images are dyadic half-open intervals. Assuming DC for the measure clauses, on Borel D subset C put nu(D)=lambda(b^{-1}(D)); this is a probability measure with nu(N_s)=2^{-|s|}. For arbitrary E subset C define nu_in(E)=sup{nu(K):K closed, K subset E} and nu_out(E)=inf{nu(O):O open, E subset O}. Then 0<=nu_in(E)<=nu_out(E)<=1 and nu_out(E)=1-nu_in(C minus E). Equality nu_in(E)=nu_out(E) implies b^{-1}(E) is Lebesgue measurable. Already in ZF, a compact Cantor copy contained in b[A], A subset [0,1), transfers to a compact Cantor copy in A. No product-measure existence theorem or AC is used.
items.proof_strategy:
DC supplies countable choice explicitly: for a sequence (X_n) of nonempty sets take the set of all finite selections f with domain n and f(i) in X_i. The relation extending by one coordinate is entire; the empty selection is a starting point. DC gives a chain whose nth term has length n; its union chooses from every X_n. This licenses exactly the countable-choice hypotheses of the published Lebesgue measure and Borel measurability results.

For binary word s of length n, recursively set I_empty=[0,1), and split each I_s=[a,a+2^{-n}) into its left/right halves I_(s0),I_(s1), always left-closed/right-open. These partition their parent. For x in [0,1), unique membership at each level defines b(x) by recursion, and b^{-1}(N_s)=I_s. If b(x)=b(y) then |x-y|<2^{-n} for every n, so x=y; the reciprocal/Archimedean bound proves 2^{-n}->0 since 2^n>=n+1. Open subsets of C are the union of their basic cylinders, a countably coded family, so their inverse images are Borel. The family of D with Borel inverse image is a sigma-algebra (inverse images commute with complements and countable unions), hence contains every Borel D. Restrict Lebesgue measure to these inverse images to define nu. Countable additivity follows directly by taking inverse images of disjoint sequences. Cylinder values are the lengths of I_s; in particular nu(C)=1. Continuity from above applies since the first set has measure at most one; continuity from below follows from the actual measure theorem. No countability of an arbitrary family of reals is being inferred.

The inner/outer definitions use nonempty bounded sets of values: empty K and O=C are admissible. Monotonicity proves the inequalities. Complementation bijects closed K subset C minus E with open O containing E, and nu(C minus K)=1-nu(K), proving the complement identity. If both bounds equal t, for each n choose closed K_n subset E and open O_n superset E with nu(O_n)-nu(K_n)<2^{-n}, using countable choice on the set of such pairs; endpoints t=0 or1 allow K_n empty or O_n=C. Put K=union K_n, O=intersection O_n. Both are Borel, K subset E subset O, and nu(O minus K)<=nu(O_n minus K_n)<2^{-n} for every n, so nu(O minus K)=0. Thus b^{-1}(E) lies between Borel b^{-1}(K) and b^{-1}(O) with null difference. Completeness of Lebesgue measure proves it measurable. This proves the needed transfer directly, without presupposing a completed coin-measure theorem.

For the last clause define pi:C->[0,1] by the unique point in the nested closures of the dyadic I_s. Equivalently it is the limit of the nondecreasing bounded dyadic left endpoints; existence uses real completeness, and the widths force uniqueness. If two inputs agree through n, their images differ by at most 2^{-n}, proving continuity. For every x, pi(b(x))=x. Hence pi is injective on b[A]. On a compact Cantor copy K subset b[A], pi is a continuous injection to R. It is a homeomorphism onto its image: compactness makes images of closed subsets compact, and compact subsets of a metric space are closed, by the finite-subcover separation argument. Therefore pi(K) is a compact Cantor copy in A. No inverse-continuity claim on all of C, nor unique binary expansion for dyadic endpoints, is used.

items.statement: In ZF+AD every subset of C, N^N or R is at most countable or contains a compact subspace homeomorphic to C. In particular every uncountable such set contains a nonempty perfect closed subset.

If its Cantor copy K is obtained, h inverse restricted to K is continuous; its image is a compact Cantor copy in A and is closed in the metrizable Baire space. In the countable case pull back the injection into N. No inference that h[A] is itself closed, nor AC-based Borel determinacy, is used. For A subset R, put A_m=(A intersect [m,m+1)) minus m, using an explicit integer enumeration. Apply the C result to b[A_m]. If some b[A_m] contains a compact Cantor copy K, the ZF coding/continuous-evaluation clause of lem-dyadic-coding-coin-measure-and-lebesgue-transfer sends K homeomorphically into A_m, and translation gives a compact Cantor copy in A. Only that lemma's ZF clause is used, not its DC measure clauses. If every b[A_m] is at most countable, then every nonempty b[A_m] has a surjective enumeration by N (invert an injection into N on its range and fill omitted indices with the value of the least used index). A sequence of binary sequences is coded by one binary sequence via the fixed pairing. For each nonempty b[A_m], its nonempty set of enumeration codes is a set of Baire reals; for an empty one use the singleton all-zero code and record that interval as empty. AD countable-real-choice selects these codes simultaneously. Decode, apply pi and translate by m, and interleave by the same pairing over nonempty intervals. If A is nonempty fill empty slots with one fixed a in A; otherwise use its empty injection. This yields a surjection from N onto A when nonempty. Assign each a its least enumeration index to get an injection A->N. Thus no unrestricted countable choice or DC is used to prove the real-line perfect-set alternative.

items.title: Winning measure-game strategies bound inner and outer measure
items.statement: In ZF+DC, for every E subset C and rational 0<v<=1, a winning I strategy in the rational measure game yields nu_in(E)>=v, and a winning II strategy yields nu_out(E)<=v. Inner and outer values are precisely the closed/open envelope values in the dyadic coding lemma.
items.proof_strategy:
For I strategy sigma, a finite bit string p is acceptable iff all its bits are positive responses when sigma is followed; the complete game history psi(p) is uniquely reconstructed. At an acceptable p define f(p) to be the current bound; at other strings set f(p)=0. The game inequality gives (f(p0)+f(p1))/2>=f(p) for every p, including unacceptable strings and their extensions. Induction gives sum_{|p|=n}2^{-n}f(p)>=v. Since 0<=f<=1 and f vanishes off the acceptable tree, the clopen union C_n of acceptable length-n cylinders has measure at least v. The C_n decrease, so the closed set C=intersection C_n has measure at least v by continuity from above. Every branch in C reconstructs a legal full sigma-play and lies in E. Thus nu_in(E)>=v.

For II strategy tau fix rational delta>0. Recursively build an acceptable bit tree and consistent histories psi(p), starting with the empty history. At an acceptable p with current rational bound v_p, let u_e be the infimum of h_e over legal rational pairs h for which tau(psi(p) followed by h)=e; set inf empty=1. Then (u_0+u_1)/2<=v_p. To prove this carefully, suppose the inequality failed. Choose rational h_e with 0<=h_e<u_e whenever u_e>0, and h_e=0 if u_e=0, close enough from below that their average still exceeds v_p. This is a legal pair in [0,1]^2. Tau must select a positive coordinate e; hence u_e>0 and h_e<u_e, contradicting the defining infimum. This repairs the unchecked subtraction u_e-epsilon at a zero coordinate in the printed argument.

Declare pe acceptable exactly when p is acceptable and u_e<1. For such e the defining set is nonempty, and choose the least code of a legal rational pair h^{p,e} producing response e and satisfying h^{p,e}_e<u_e+delta*2^{-(|p|+1)}. Such a pair exists by the infimum property. Define psi(pe) by that actual pair and response. Every chosen response is positive by legality. No arbitrary choice of a real move is used; least rational codes make the recursive rule single-valued. At acceptable p set f(p)=v_p; at other p set f(p)=1. For excluded children u_e=1, so f(pe)=1<=u_e+delta*2^{-(|p|+1)}. Hence at length n the average child value is <=f(p)+delta*2^{-(n+1)}; for an unacceptable p both children have f=1 and the same inequality holds. Induction gives sum_{|p|=n}2^{-n}f(p)<=v+delta*(1-2^{-n}). The clopen union U_n of unacceptable length-n cylinders therefore has measure <=v+delta*(1-2^{-n}), since f is nonnegative and equals one there. These U_n increase. Every branch outside their union reconstructs an infinite tau-play and lies outside E. Thus U=union U_n is an open superset of E with nu(U)<=v+delta by continuity from below. It follows nu_out(E)<=v+delta for every positive rational delta, hence <=v. All uses of nu and continuity are supplied by the previous lemma under DC; no regularity theorem for arbitrary E was assumed.

items.title: Under AD and DC every real set is Lebesgue measurable
items.statement: In ZF+AD+DC every subset of R is Lebesgue measurable. DC is separately assumed, not deduced from AD; no AC-based theorem of determinacy, analytic regularity, or recorded-not-proved result is consumed.
items.proof_strategy:
For E subset C, AD determines each rational measure game by its explicit natural-number coding. If nu_in(E)<nu_out(E), rational density gives v strictly between them with 0<v<=1. I winning would imply nu_in(E)>=v and II winning would imply nu_out(E)<=v; both contradict the choice of v. Thus the two values agree. The dyadic transfer lemma implies b^{-1}(E) is Lebesgue measurable.

For arbitrary A subset [0,1), take E=b[A]. The coding b is injective, so b^{-1}(E)=A. Thus every subset of [0,1) is measurable. For any A subset R, the translates A_m=(A intersect [m,m+1)) minus m, m integer, lie in [0,1) and are measurable. Translation invariance gives measurability of A_m+m. Enumerate the integers explicitly as 0,1,-1,2,-2,...; their union is A because the Archimedean property puts every real in one such unit interval. The Lebesgue sigma-algebra, available from DC's countable choice in the interface lemma, is closed under this sequence of unions. Hence A is measurable. This uses a defined family, not choices of per-interval measures or sets.

items.statement: False assertion: every subset of R is Borel. In ZFC there is an undetermined payoff A subset N^N; for the earlier continuous injection e:N^N -> R, the subset e[A] is not Borel in R.
items.proof_strategy: Take the A supplied by the earlier AC strategy-diagonalization theorem. If e[A] were Borel, continuous pullback would make e^(-1)(e[A]) Borel in N^N. items.statement: For an enumerated basis (U_n), the one-node leaf(n) code evaluates to U_n, a complement root with its sole child leaf(n) evaluates to X minus U_n, a union root with no children evaluates to the empty set, and a complement above that empty union evaluates to X.
